meta.name: PLA
meta.description: PLA — migrated verbatim from tools/material_db.json (typical desktop-FDM datasheet-class values) plus the heat-set pull-out table from joint_check.py. Poisson is a typical thermoplastic value (absent from material_db). Thermal-transport fields are null: not present in the migrated source, not invented.

sn_curve.note: engineering rule of thumb (~1e6-cycle allowable = ultimate x knockdown), NOT a measured S-N curve

anisotropy.model: scalar-tier direction heuristic (production_check.py): across-layer (Z) tensile strength / in-plane (XY) strength; applied when the primary load is > threshold deg out of the layer plane

heatset_pullout_n.note: brass knurled heat-set at standard insert length; conservative low ends (joint_check.py)

sources.mechanical.poisson: typical thermoplastic (material_db.json has no poisson); provided for FEA
sources._db_source_note: typical of Prusament/Ultimaker PLA datasheets (tensile 50-60 MPa, E 2.9-3.6 GPa, HDT-B 55-60 C). Creep fraction set LOW (0.2): PLA cold-flows measurably at room temperature under sustained load.
sources.thermal.conductivity_w_mk: 0.13 W/mK, conservative-low of the printed+handbook band 0.12-0.25: measured PRINTED PLA 0.12 (transparent) / 0.15-0.25 (pigmented), AIP Conf. Proc. 2305:020022 https://pubs.aip.org/aip/acp/article/2305/1/020022/740039 ; handbook lineage 0.13 https://www.makeitfrom.com/material-properties/Polylactic-Acid-PLA-Polylactide (Xometry/SEAS3D TDS repeat this lineage verbatim — counted once); printed-PLA study uses lit. 0.16 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9141791/
sources.thermal.specific_heat_j_kgk: 1200 J/kgK at room temperature (conservative for heating-rate gates): measured printed PLA cp 1200 (transparent) / 900-1100 (pigmented) at RT, AIP Conf. Proc. 2305:020022 https://pubs.aip.org/aip/acp/article/2305/1/020022/740039 and https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AIPC.2894b0010M/abstract ; the widely-quoted 1800 (MakeItFrom/Xometry lineage https://www.makeitfrom.com/material-properties/Polylactic-Acid-PLA-Polylactide) is likely a nearer-melt value — see conflicts
sources.thermal.tg_or_melt_c: Tg 60 C (DSC): Polymaker PolyLite PLA TDS Tg 61 https://wiki.polymaker.com/polymaker-products/more-about-our-products/documents/technical-data-sheets/pla/polylite-tm-pla ; Bambu PLA Basic TDS Tg 60 https://wiki.bambulab.com/filament-acc/abs-asa-pc/bambu_pla_basic_technical_data_sheet.pdf
sources.thermal.softening_c: softening_c = conservative softening allowable for sustained-load design: the LOW end of min(Tg, HDT-B 0.45 MPa) across cited brand TDS values for this material class (degC). PLA: 55 C = low end of HDT-B 55-60: Prusament PLA TDS HDT 0.45 MPa = 55 C (ISO 75) https://prusament.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/PLA_Prusament_TDS_2021_10_EN.pdf ; Bambu PLA Basic 57 C; Polymaker PolyLite 60 C (URLs above)
sources.thermal._printed_anisotropy_note: printed parts conduct WORSE than bulk, direction-dependent: inter-layer thermal contact resistance dominates through-thickness conduction (Prajapati et al., Additive Manufacturing 2018, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2214860417305456); voids/porosity measurably reduce heat transmission even at 100% infill (Entropy 24:654 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9141791/); through-plane k reported ~20-40% below in-plane in FDM literature (secondary synthesis, primaries paywalled — treat percentage as indicative). Records store the conservative-LOW isotropic value.
sources.thermal._cp_temperature_note: cp is strongly temperature-dependent (amorphous polymers jump +30-50% crossing Tg; Covestro shows TPU cp +~15% from 20C to 80C) — record values are ROOM-TEMPERATURE-class unless noted
sources.creep: entire block derived 2026-07-30 from the cited data_anchors/model_constants URLs inside the block itself; construction chain in creep.derivation; printed-specimen data preferred, bulk analogs flagged inline

conflicts.note: RT DSC measurements of printed PLA cluster 900-1200 J/kgK; 1800 is plausible approaching melt (cp rises steeply with T). Canonical keeps the RT-measured, conservative (faster-heating) value.

the legacy blanket 'sustained = 20% of ultimate' (12 MPa) is NOT supported at year scale by any published printed-PLA data; the creep table gives 2.5 MPa at 1 y / 23 C. Migrating production_check-class consumers from the scalar fraction to the table changes allowables — a human physics decision, surfaced here instead of silently made.

creep.basis: time-derated SUSTAINED-stress allowables for PRINTED (FDM) PLA, in-plane loading, unannealed, dry, constant load. Conservative CONSTRUCTION from published creep/rupture data (chain in 'derivation'), NOT a measured design curve: safety factor 2.0 on the worst measured printed rupture, iso-deformation time-derating from the only quantified printed creep-compliance history, all values rounded DOWN to 0.5 MPa steps. Across-layer (Z) loads: multiply by process.anisotropy.z_vs_xy_strength_ratio (0.55) on top.

23C.1h: Medium — bracketed by measured printed rupture (15 MPa fails ~2 h) and no-rupture (20 MPa holds 3 h) data
23C.24h: Medium-Low — one-decade extrapolation between measured anchors
23C.30d: Low — extrapolation; no printed-PLA dataset longer than ~170 h found (2026-07-30)
23C.1y: Low — extrapolation; physical aging (which SLOWS creep) ignored, so bias is conservative

55C.1h: Low-Medium — WLF-shifted from measured 60 C rupture; PLA is mid-glass-transition here
55C.24h: Low — only analog is a CRYSTALLIZED BULK grade surviving 7.5 d at 3 MPa/60 C with ~3.5x deformation growth
55C.30d: BOUND, not a measurement — no experimental support for ANY allowable above ~0.5 MPa at 55 C beyond days
55C.1y: BOUND, not a measurement — treat as 'do not design sustained load into unannealed PLA at 55 C'

derivation: ANCHOR RT rupture: printed PLA tensile creep-rupture at 15 MPa / 25 C fails in 1.18-2.25 h across all 39 print configs (Waseem 2020, only printed RT rupture dataset). Conflicts with Dogan 2022 (20 MPa / 25 C holds 3 h, no rupture) — conflict kept as data, WORST case governs.

RT 1 h allowable = 15 MPa worst measured rupture / SF 2.0 = 7.5 MPa. Cross-checks: 10 MPa / 25 C holds 3 h with secondary creep only (Dogan); 10 MPa long-term on porous printed scaffolds without shape change (Niaza 2017).

time-derating per decade: the only quantified printed-PLA creep history — flexural creep modulus falls to 56% of static over 170 h at ~4.8 MPa (Fischbach 2023) = compliance x1.79 over ~2.3 decades = x1.29/decade. Iso-deformation allowable divides by that factor per decade of load duration.

RT column: 1h 7.5 -> 24h 7.5/1.29^1.4 = 5.2 -> 5.0 · 30d 7.5/1.29^2.9 = 3.6 -> 3.5 · 1y 7.5/1.29^3.9 = 2.8 -> 2.5 MPa (rounded DOWN). Physical aging slows creep (shift-rate mu ~ 0.72, Fischbach), so ignoring it is conservative.

ANCHOR hot rupture: printed PLA at 60 C ruptures at 10 MPa in < 3 h and at 20 MPa in minutes (Dogan 2022). WLF for PLA (C1 19.4, C2 148.3 K at Tref 60 C; Kontou 2024) gives aT(55->60) ~ 4.8: damage at 55 C runs ~5x slower than 60 C.

55 C 1 h = 10 MPa (60 C rupture stress) / SF ~3.3 = 3.0 MPa (extra margin because 55 C sits INSIDE the glass transition: DSC Tg 55-60 C, compression yield already halves 80->40 MPa by 50 C, Slavkovic 2024).

55 C 24 h = 1.5 MPa: half of the 3 MPa that survived 7.5 d at 60 C — but that analog is a CRYSTALLIZING BULK grade with ~3.5x deformation growth (Morreale 2017); unannealed printed PLA is strictly worse.

55 C 30 d / 1 y = 0.5 MPa as a stated BOUND: storage modulus above Tg collapses to ~1-6 MPa (Issabayeva 2023, Slavkovic 2024) and HDT at 0.45 MPa IS 55 C (NatureWorks 4043D TDS) — i.e. the standard itself deflects at 0.45 MPa there. No experiment supports more; UNKNOWN is the first-class answer above this line.

data_anchors.outcome: no rupture, most creep of tested polymers
creep modulus -> 56% of static, still creeping; aging shift-rate mu ~ 0.72
data_anchors.specimen: printed (flexural, stress derived from ISO 178 geometry)
BULK crystallizing grade (not printed) — analog only

arrhenius_sub_tg.note: steady-state creep, bulk PLA; ~3.6x rate per +10 C near RT (transient 59.4)

findley_decade_factor.note: compliance growth per decade of time, from the 170 h printed flexural test — the derating engine of this table

gaps_unknowns: NO creep-rupture data for printed PLA at 50-60 C beyond hours; nothing at 30 d or 1 y at any stress — the 55 C long-duration cells are bounds, not measurements
NO printed-PLA RT dataset longer than 170 h found (a >1000 h program exists but its numbers are paywalled: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11029-026-10331-z)
RT rupture conflict unresolved: Waseem 15 MPa/~2 h rupture vs Dogan 20 MPa/3 h no-rupture — worst case kept as governing
humidity/hydrolysis coupling at 55 C flagged significant but quantified nowhere for printed PLA

annealing (90 C/2 h) improves creep resistance ~1.85x at 47 C and crystallized grades push HDT to ~144 C — but NO long-duration creep data for annealed printed PLA either; note the trap: sub-Tg 50 C/8 h 'annealing' without crystallization CUT strength 25-29% (Bertocco 2022)
build-orientation creep effect measured qualitatively (Y-90 lower creep strength) but not tabulated — hence the flat z-ratio multiplier
